predictions.experiment: Paired tail-rate ratio on hard328: the pooled rate of sampled tokens with p < 0.01 per generated token, RL plain over base cue, on problems both models finished. This tests the mechanism against tail trimming: the rival r3-surprises-1 (RL trims the tail everywhere) predicts about 0.6 or less, and this mechanism predicts about 1.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain), fetched with the aws commands in inventory.md. In each file keep one row per problem_index: the one with the smallest attempt, or the first in file order if there is no attempt field. Keep the problem_index values present in both files whose kept rows have cap_hit false in both files. Drop a problem from both models if either row has a null or missing n_tok_p_lt_1e2 or n_generated, or n_generated == 0. For each model, rate = sum of n_tok_p_lt_1e2 / sum of n_generated over the kept problems, pooled, not a mean of per-row rates. Statistic = rate(86ef) / rate(e72c). No grading is used.

predictions.note: Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01 e72c (base cue) and 86ef (RL plain) answers.jsonl, fetched to runs/theory-tests/r5/day1_hard328-01/<job>/answers.jsonl. Neither file has the field n_tok_p_lt_1e2 in any of its 328 rows (I checked field names only; the day1 jobs predate the run_cell.py change that writes it), so the script prints not_computable. The 'drop a problem if the field is missing' clause, read literally, would drop every problem and leave 0/0, which is also not computable; I did not count that as refuted. If the field were present: one row per problem_index (smallest attempt, else first in file order; neither file has an attempt field), cap_hit must be exactly False in both files, ratio of pooled rates, bootstrap over paired problems. alt_measured = ratio of the mean per-row rates.

predictions.experiment: Cause: whether the cued base's wrong answers carry more low-probability tokens than its right ones at matched length, on hard328. This mechanism (errors are drawn from the head) predicts a ratio near 1. A tail-derailment account (unlikely tokens push answers off course) predicts about 1.3 or more.
predictions.recipe: File: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue). Keep one row per problem_index (smallest attempt, else first in file order). Keep rows with cap_hit false, non-null n_tok_p_lt_1e2 and n_generated > 0. Right = score_v3 == 1, and wrong = any other value, with null counting as wrong. Sort the kept rows by n_generated ascending, ties broken by problem_index ascending. Give each row its 0-based rank r and quartile q = floor(4*r/N), where N is the number of kept rows. In each quartile compute rW = sum n_tok_p_lt_1e2 / sum n_generated over the wrong rows and rR the same over the right rows. Skip a quartile with no wrong rows, no right rows, or rR == 0. ratio_q = rW / rR. Statistic = sum over kept quartiles of (number of wrong rows in q) * ratio_q / sum over kept quartiles of (number of wrong rows in q).
predictions.unit: ratio of pooled rates (wrong / right), wrong-count-weighted over length quartiles

predictions.note: File: e72c answers.jsonl only. Same missing field n_tok_p_lt_1e2, so the result is not_computable. If the field were present: wrong = score_v3 != 1 (null counts as wrong), quartile = floor(4r/N) over rows sorted by (n_generated, problem_index), skip a quartile with no wrong rows, no right rows or rR == 0, average ratio_q weighted by wrong count. The bootstrap resamples rows and rebuilds the quartiles each time. n = the smaller of the wrong and right groups. alt_measured = one pooled wrong/right ratio with no length matching.

predictions.experiment: Where the effect should not appear: on hard328 problems where the cued base finished wrong and RL finished, whether RL's tail-rate change relative to the base differs between problems RL fixes and problems it does not. The tail-trimming rival puts the fix where the tail was cut, a clearly negative difference of about -0.3. This mechanism (fixes come from head swaps) predicts about 0.
predictions.recipe: Files: e72c (base cue) and 86ef (RL plain) answers.jsonl as in the first prediction, one row per problem_index each (smallest attempt, else first in file order). Keep problems present in both files where the e72c row has cap_hit false and score_v3 != 1 (null counts as not 1), and the 86ef row has cap_hit false. Drop a problem if either row has a null or missing n_tok_p_lt_1e2 or n_generated, or n_generated == 0. Per problem d = ln((t_RL + 0.5) / g_RL) - ln((t_b + 0.5) / g_b), with t = n_tok_p_lt_1e2 and g = n_generated of that model's row. Fixed = 86ef score_v3 == 1, and unfixed = otherwise. Statistic = (mean d over fixed problems) - (mean d over unfixed problems). If either group is empty, the statistic counts as refuted.
predictions.unit: difference of mean natural-log rate ratios
predictions.refuted_by: statistic below -0.25 or above 0.25, or either group empty
